keyQuotes: AI has started to shift from 'answering questions' to genuinely 'getting a piece of work done for people.'
The expansion path of Codex is moving from people who write code to people who handle documents, data, research, sales, recruiting, legal, and operations.
When models can call tools, read and write files, and execute tasks, risks will enter real workflows.

mainPoints.explanation: The article cites the OpenAI report, noting that in the ChatGPT era, nearly half of usage was asking questions, whereas Codex enables users to use AI to execute tasks like debugging, refactoring, and environment setup, fundamentally changing the usage paradigm.
mainPoints.point: AI is shifting from 'answering questions' to 'getting work done for people,' and Codex is a prime example.

mainPoints.explanation: 97.9% of active employees use Codex, and Codex output tokens account for 99.8% of the total; power users run it for over 60 hours daily on average, indicating that the agent is deeply embedded into daily workflows.
mainPoints.point: Over 90% of the workload for OpenAI internal employees is now handled by Codex, achieving near-full adoption.

mainPoints.explanation: Among external organizations, active non-developer Codex users grew 189 times, and among individual users, 130 times. Usage in roles like legal, recruiting, and operations is rising rapidly, showing the agent is breaking beyond coding boundaries.
mainPoints.point: Codex users are rapidly expanding from developers to non-developers.

mainPoints.explanation: The proportion of users submitting tasks that take a skilled human over 1 hour doubled in six months, with 25.6% of users attempting heavy tasks lasting over 8 hours; skill usage rose from 5.4% to 26.6%, indicating users are automating repetitive work.
mainPoints.point: Task complexity and concurrency continue to climb, and users are starting to accumulate reusable workflows.

oneSentenceSummary: Based on data from the OpenAI Codex research report, this article illustrates the paradigm shift of AI agents from answering questions to executing work, reveals that over 90% of internal workloads at OpenAI are now handled by Codex, highlights the explosive growth among non-developers and rising task complexity, and explores the implications for AI regulation.
originalTitle: 你的 Codex 可能只解锁了 1%，大神让它一天肝 71 小时
summary: Using the release of the OpenAI Codex usage report as a starting point, and set against the backdrop of the U.S. government requesting restrictions on the release of GPT-5.6, this article provides an in-depth analysis of how the AI agent product Codex is transforming the way we work. Report data shows: 97.9% of active OpenAI employees use Codex, with over 90% of their workload completed by Codex on average; among external organizations, the usage by non-developers has grown by over a hundredfold, expanding Codex from a developer tool to roles in legal, recruiting, and operations; users are submitting increasingly heavy tasks (the proportion of tasks that would take a skilled human over 1 hour rose from 35% to 70%), and running multiple agents concurrently has become the norm (peaking at 71 hours of daily runtime); users are beginning to accumulate reusable workflows (skill usage rate climbed to 26.6%). The article points out that as AI shifts from conversation to execution, risks enter real workflows and regulatory sensitivity rises accordingly—the phased release of GPT-5.6 is a direct reflection of this logic.
title: Your Codex May Only Be 1% Unlocked: Power Users Run It 71 Hours a Day
